assumptions: CP-094, MEASURED IN FOUR PARTS, each independently assertable. (1) ONE ACCOUNTABLE MANAGER PER DEPARTMENT is `workforce_department_managers_one_accountable_uidx`, a PARTIAL UNIQUE INDEX on (department_id) where ended_at is null. An INDEX, not a trigger and not a CHECK, because an index is what the database enforces under concurrency - two simultaneous appointments produced exactly 1 row and at least one 23505, and with the index dropped the same two both succeeded. (2) ONE ACTIVE PRIMARY MEMBERSHIP PER (ORGANIZATION, PERSON) is `workforce_department_memberships_one_active_primary_uidx`, partial on (org_id, person_user_id) where membership_kind='primary' and is_active and effective_to is null. Per ORGANIZATION, not globally: a person who genuinely works for two organizations is primary in each. Measured under the same two-session race with the same drop-the-index control. (3) SECONDARY MEMBERSHIP NEVER CONFERS MANAGEMENT AUTHORITY, in the database and not only in the resolver - see the dedicated assumption below. (4) ORGANIZATION ADMINISTRATORS RETAIN ORGANIZATION-WIDE AUTHORITY: every write arm admits has_perm(uid, org_id, 'workforce.manage'), measured as an org A administrator reading all of org A's departments and 0 of org B's, creating a department in their own org, and STILL being unable to appoint a manager of org B's department because the composite foreign key binds the two columns.

HOW 'SECONDARY NEVER CONFERS MANAGEMENT AUTHORITY' IS ENFORCED IN THE DATABASE, since that is the criterion most likely to be satisfied by a comment. Three structural facts, each independently assertable, none of them prose. (a) `public.workforce_department_is_managed_by` is the ONLY authority predicate any policy or view in this file uses for department scope, and its body reads workforce_department_managers and NEVER workforce_department_memberships. The contract postflight asserts the ABSENCE of that table name in pg_get_functiondef, and the harness INJECTS the widening edit and requires the postflight to report it - so a future edit that adds the table name is a failed apply, not a review note. (b) The management relation's INSERT and UPDATE policies require organization-wide workforce.manage, which DB-016 deliberately does NOT grant to department_manager (WFC-003 §2.5.2: seed(role) = catalog(role) ∩ workforce.* − departmentScoped(role), with DEPARTMENT_SCOPED_ROLE_CAPABILITIES at lib/auth/admin-capabilities.ts:319-323 withholding it). MEASURED on the extracted matrix: has_perm(department_manager, org, 'workforce.manage') is FALSE. A worker therefore cannot promote themselves by writing a row, and the harness measures both halves: the predicate returns FALSE for a secondary-only member, and their INSERT into the manager relation is refused 42501. (c) There is no DELETE policy and no DELETE privilege on either management or membership relation, for authenticated, anon AND service_role - the first revision granted `all` to service_role and the postflight reported it, which was a real bypass.

A DEPARTMENT MANAGER MAY EDIT THEIR DEPARTMENT AND NOT ITS TENANT BOUNDARY - and the obvious way to express it in RLS IS WRONG, which only executing it revealed. The first revision made `wfc004_workforce_departments_update` deliberately ASYMMETRIC: using admitted a department manager, with check did not, reasoning that this would let them change name and slug but not org_id, department_kind or vendor_entity_id. The harness measured a department manager's RENAME of their own department being REFUSED with 42501, because an RLS `with check` is a ROW-level predicate and has no way to say 'this change is fine, that column is not'. The asymmetry granted the resource scope CP-094 requires and then took it away again on the first legitimate write, which is worse than not offering it. The corrected design splits the two concerns by the mechanism that can carry each: RLS answers 'may this caller modify this ROW?' symmetrically (org-wide manage OR the manager relation), and a SECURITY INVOKER BEFORE UPDATE trigger, workforce_departments_protect_boundaries, answers 'may this caller modify these COLUMNS?' for org_id, department_kind and vendor_entity_id. Both halves are measured and both are asserted by the postflight, because either alone is a defect: a symmetric policy without the trigger would let a manager re-point their own org_id, and the asymmetric policy refuses a legitimate rename. The trigger is conditional on a JWT being present so a migration or operator tool can still perform a deliberate re-scope, distinguishable by the absence of a session rather than by a null column - the same rule the CP-095 actor trigger uses.

AN RLS-FILTERED WRITE IS A SILENT NO-OP, NOT A DENIAL, AND THIS IS THE MOST OPERATIONALLY IMPORTANT FACT THIS FILE PRODUCES. The harness's first revision asserted on the psql exit code and reported two `rc=0` failures that were both SUCCEEDS: a secondary-only member's UPDATE of a department and their INSERT into the ledger both exited 0 having written nothing. PostgreSQL applies a policy by FILTERING candidate rows, so `update ... where id = X` matches zero visible rows, updates zero rows and exits 0; and an `insert ... select` whose own SELECT is RLS-filtered to zero rows inserts nothing and exits 0. This is CP-110's plausible zero arriving through RLS rather than through a capability gate, and it is worse than a denial because a caller cannot tell it from success. Every write assertion in the harness therefore counts AFFECTED ROWS (through a data-modifying CTE, because psql -q suppresses the `UPDATE n` tag) and pairs each 0-row result with the positive 1-row result for a different caller. ROUTED as HF-WFC-004-AFFECTED-ROW-COUNT: WFC-005's command layer must check affected-row counts and must not report a save from a 0-row write. The `not_authorized` state in WFC-008..010 must be produced from the row count, not from the absence of an error.

A NEW GRANT DEPENDENCY, NEW IN THIS PROGRAM, FOUND BY EXECUTING IT. The self-keyed arm of `wfc004_workforce_department_memberships_select` calls `auth.uid()` DIRECTLY: `or (person_user_id = (select auth.uid()) and is_active and effective_to is null)`. A direct auth.uid() is evaluated as the CALLER, unlike the auth.uid() inside has_perm / is_org_member, which are SECURITY DEFINER and resolve as their owner. So this arm requires `authenticated` to hold USAGE on the `auth` SCHEMA - a schema-level privilege, not a table-level one, and a dependency class none of DB-013's predicates had. The harness measured `permission denied for schema auth` on its first run. Supabase grants it on every project, so it is invisible in this repository and invisible to a reader of a policy. The arm is KEPT: a worker who cannot read their own department placement cannot answer 'which department am I in'. Carried as a labelled preflight probe with a stop condition, not assumed.

DB-013's `organizations` SELECT GRANT DEPENDENCY is inherited knowingly. Every predicate carries `exists (select 1 from public.organizations organization where organization.id = <rel>.org_id)` as defence in depth, modelled on DB-013's staff_members_scoped_* (:71-97). That subquery is RLS-evaluated as the caller, so it needs table-level SELECT on public.organizations, which this chain does not manage in SQL. PostgreSQL does not guarantee short-circuit evaluation of an OR, so the requirement is WHOLE-RELATION rather than per-arm: the self-keyed arm is OR'd against the EXISTS branch and still failed with `permission denied for table organizations`. Without the grant the policies DENY (fail closed, never open) and the symptom is a functional false-denial. This is DB-013's recorded surprise, measured again rather than assumed.

NO NEW AUTHORITY MECHANISM. Every organization-scoped predicate calls the chain's own public.has_perm (20260821180438:122-151). Every active-manager validation calls the chain's own public.is_org_member (20260821180438:106-120), which is the same SECURITY DEFINER 20260825131000:68-71 already uses. No second membership table is introduced and `staff_members.status` is never consulted for activity (WFC-003 §6.3). `org_role_permissions` is NOT re-seeded: the `workforce.*` slice is WFC-003 §2.5.2's decision and DB-016's SQL (20260926200000), and re-writing it would invalidate every active acting-context session a second time, because capability_version digests perms IN ORDER (20260722002848:180-183,317-320).

STATED RESIDUAL, DELIBERATELY NOT NARROWED HERE: `workforce.view` is seeded organization-wide for eight roles including department_manager (DB-016), so the first two conjuncts of the department SELECT policy already admit a department manager to every department row in their organization. WFC-003 §2.5.2 records that residual as belonging to WFC-005/WFC-006, which own the read models. The one-line change that would close it is to drop the has_perm(view) arm; it is NOT made in a schema task because it is a read-model decision and making it here would silently remove a surface those lanes have not yet replaced. A department row carries name, slug, kind and a vendor_entity_id, and the vendor entity itself stays behind vendor.view, so the residual exposes no vendor data. Stated on the policy's COMMENT as well as here.

STATED LIMIT, NOT AN OVERSTATEMENT OF ENFORCEMENT: 'at most one active primary membership per (organization, person)' is enforced by an index and proven under concurrency. 'At least one' is a property of a SET of rows and is NOT enforced: demoting the last active primary to secondary would leave a worker with none, and a per-row index cannot see the other rows. It is DETECTED rather than prevented, by `public.workforce_membership_health` (a security_invoker view reporting active_primary_count per organization/person), and prevented at the command layer, which is WFC-005's. A deferred cross-row constraint trigger was considered and rejected: it would fire on every membership write including bulk imports and would make a legitimate reorganisation a two-phase operation.

DELIBERATELY NOT STORED: there is no `manager_state` or `has_manager` column on workforce_departments. A denormalised flag would need an AFTER trigger to write the parent row, and under `force row level security` that write depends on whether the role executing the migration holds BYPASSRLS - a HOST-DEPENDENT property, not a schema property, and therefore not something this file may assume. `public.workforce_department_directory` exposes the same fact as a security_invoker view over an index-only subquery against the partial unique index, which is at most one row and cannot drift. The invariant CP-094 protects then has exactly one representation in the database, and it is the one the index enforces. `manager_user_id IS NULL` is the honest representation of a department with no accountable manager yet, and it is never filled in by inference (CP-094).

NO `information_schema.tables` EXISTENCE GUARD APPEARS IN THIS FILE, so the CP-109 ordering trap is not reachable: all three relations are created here at a version later than anything that references them, and the two indexes that later migrations depend on are created here. `node supabase/tests/wfc004_guarded_block_order.mjs` MEASURES that absence against the real 315-migration chain and its self-test proves the instrument can fail - it must find the chain's 12 never-executed guards, including the confirmed 20250812093500 over staff_performance_metrics, and it must report the same guard as running when evaluated at a later version position.

Every existing row is preserved. No pre-existing relation is created, altered or dropped; no pre-existing column is touched; no pre-existing data row is read for update or deleted. The free-text `department` columns are NOT dropped, NOT backfilled into departments and NOT compared by value: they are read only to produce reviewable reconciliation rows in 20260927100200, because WFC-003 §6.9 requires the department entity to replace them by explicit LINK, never by value comparison, and records reading them as a scope as DEPARTMENT_SCOPE_FORBIDDEN_WORKAROUND. NO backfill of departments or memberships happens in this file at all, and the harness MEASURES that: re-applying over two free-text department strings, one org-less staff row, one name-only vendor contract, one name-only event request, one tour-scoped vendor and one tenant-less staffing agency created ZERO departments and ZERO memberships.

lib/database.types.ts is byte-unchanged and this migration DOES require a type regeneration: it creates three tables, one view, two further views and two functions that the contract does not declare. Regeneration is blocked (CP-089, CP-092) and is not attempted. The exact specification of what regeneration must produce is in this manifest and in the task record, so a blocked regeneration is not mistaken for a schema that needs no types.
layeredPlan: Layer 0 (preflight, read-only, operator). Run the Layer 0 queries and record every result. Five things decide whether this file is correct for THIS target: (a) `has_table_privilege('authenticated','public.organizations','select')` and `has_schema_privilege('authenticated','auth','usage')` - if either is false, every policy here DENIES and the only visible effect of the apply is that workforce reads return nothing, so stop and report. (b) the full policy set on staff_members, staff_shifts and staff_performance_metrics - this file does not touch them, and if any of them still carries a permissive predecessor the department schema is not the place to fix it; route it rather than improvising a drop in the same run. (c) `select role, perms from public.org_role_permissions order by role` and, for each row that is a member of the acting organization, that member's `status` - the resource-scoped arms depend on a live manager row, and a target whose members are mostly `invited` will read as 'no department managers exist'. (d) how many `org_members` rows have status <> 'active' for the acting organization - the resource scope is defined over ACTIVE managers only, and an operator should be able to say out loud how many departments will therefore be managerless. (e) `has_function_privilege('authenticated','public.is_org_member(uuid,uuid)','execute')` - the manager-validity trigger calls it, and without EXECUTE the trigger fails closed and NO manager row can be created.

Layer 1 (apply, single run, operator). One transaction, explicit, this file only - never `supabase db reset`, never `db push --include-all`, never a chain replay (CP-051). Three CREATE TABLE, one CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION, four CREATE UNIQUE/CREATE INDEX, three RLS enable+force, ten DROP+CREATE POLICY, two CREATE OR REPLACE TRIGGER FUNCTION, two CREATE TRIGGER (each preceded by DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS), one updated_at toucher with its trigger, the grant/revoke block, two CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW with (security_invoker = true), and a DO block that RAISEs unless: all three relations exist with RLS enabled AND forced; all ten required policies exist on the right command, permissive and not anon/PUBLIC-reachable; NO delete or FOR-ALL policy exists on the manager or membership relations; no DELETE privilege is held on them by authenticated; anon holds no privilege on any of the three; no policy carries an unconditional clause, branching on polcmd; both views are security_invoker; the department-scope function does not name the membership relation; both required partial unique indexes exist WITH their WHERE clauses; the manager active-membership trigger exists; the manager INSERT policy has NO department-scoped arm; the department UPDATE policy carries the manager arm on BOTH clauses; and the boundary-column trigger exists. The post-condition is inside the same transaction as the change, so a target that cannot reach the asserted state fails the apply instead of reporting success. A CORRECT RESULT INCLUDES a failed apply from any of those assertions, which means the target's state differs from what this file was written against and the difference must be understood before retrying.

Layer 2 (postflight, read-only, operator). Run `psql -f supabase/tests/wfc004_workforce_departments_contract.sql`; expect ZERO violation rows and exactly one summary row rendering `WFC-004 workforce departments|t|0`. Then the labelled caller probes, as at least SIX different identities, because the resource-scoped arms make the answer caller-dependent and a probe run as the wrong identity is not evidence: an organization administrator, a department_manager who IS an appointed manager of one department, a department_manager who is NOT, a worker with a primary membership, a worker with a secondary membership only, and a revoked member. WHAT A CORRECT DENIAL LOOKS LIKE: a department manager reading 0 of the OTHER organization's departments is correct; a secondary-only member updating a department and receiving `UPDATE 0` with exit 0 is correct AND is the silent-no-op fact, so the probe must read the row count, not the exit code. 'The policies were already in place' is not a possible outcome for this file - these are new relations - so a postflight that reports violations on a correctly applied target means the apply did not complete, and the file is one transaction so that cannot be partial.

Layer 3 (no fourth layer in this lane). Seven items are ROUTED rather than absorbed: the vendors/org_vendors merge (20260927100000's recorded unresolved decision), the department_manager read-scope narrowing (WFC-005/WFC-006's read-model call), the affected-row-count requirement on every write command (WFC-005), the CP-103 parity surface of the seven live `app/api/admin/workforce/**` routes (WFC-005/WFC-006), staffing_agencies as vendors (20260927100200 quarantines it), the vendor.* matrix provisioning (WFC-003 under CP-102), and the `is_org_member` predicate not being enforced at seven live read sites (WORK-102's). None is required for this file to be safe.

rowCountQueries: SELECT c.relname, c.relkind, c.relrowsecurity, c.relforcerowsecurity FROM pg_class c JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace WHERE n.nspname = 'public' AND c.relname IN ('workforce_departments','workforce_department_managers','workforce_department_memberships') ORDER BY c.relname

SELECT has_table_privilege('authenticated','public.organizations','select') AS authenticated_can_select_organizations, has_schema_privilege('authenticated','auth','usage') AS authenticated_can_use_auth_schema, has_function_privilege('authenticated','public.is_org_member(uuid,uuid)','execute') AS authenticated_can_execute_is_org_member, has_function_privilege('authenticated','public.has_perm(uuid,uuid,text)','execute') AS authenticated_can_execute_has_perm

SELECT p.polname, p.polcmd, p.polpermissive, p.polroles::regrole[], pg_get_expr(p.polqual, p.polrelid) AS using_expr, pg_get_expr(p.polwithcheck, p.polrelid) AS check_expr FROM pg_policy p JOIN pg_class c ON c.oid = p.polrelid JOIN pg_namespace n ON n.oid = c.relnamespace WHERE n.nspname = 'public' AND c.relname IN ('staff_members','staff_shifts','staff_performance_metrics') ORDER BY c.relname, p.polcmd, p.polname
SELECT om.status, count(*) FROM public.org_members om WHERE om.org_id = '<THE ACTING ORGANIZATION>' GROUP BY om.status ORDER BY om.status
SELECT role, perms FROM public.org_role_permissions ORDER BY role
SELECT count(*) AS departments_that_would_be_managerless FROM (SELECT DISTINCT om.org_id FROM public.org_members om WHERE om.status = 'active') live_orgs

SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'active') AS active_members, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'invited') AS invited_members, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'revoked') AS revoked_members FROM public.org_members

SELECT count(*) AS staff_members_rows, count(*) FILTER (WHERE department IS NOT NULL AND btrim(department) <> '') AS staff_rows_with_a_free_text_department, count(DISTINCT btrim(department)) FILTER (WHERE department IS NOT NULL AND btrim(department) <> '') AS distinct_free_text_department_values FROM public.staff_members
SELECT to_regclass('public.vendor_entities') AS vendor_entities_exists, to_regclass('public.vendors') AS vendors_exists, to_regclass('public.org_vendors') AS org_vendors_exists
preflight.expectedAffectedRows: Zero pre-existing data rows are changed. Three tables are created with their indexes, one function and two trigger functions, two triggers, ten policies and two views. No pre-existing relation, column, index, constraint, trigger or function is created, altered or dropped. No data row is read for update or deleted. The only rows this file writes are rows in the three NEW tables, and it writes none at apply time - the reconciliation backfill is 20260927100200's.

execution.resumeStrategy: Authored - manual apply pending (CP-051). One transaction, one file. The three CREATE TABLE take ACCESS EXCLUSIVE locks only on relations that do not yet exist, so there is no contention with a live table. The indexes are on new tables. DROP TRIGGER and CREATE TRIGGER take a brief exclusive lock on the new table only. DROP POLICY and CREATE POLICY take locks on catalog rows, not on any table's data. No table is rewritten, re-indexed or re-vacuumed, so there is no lock-budget risk from the data side. Safe to apply BEFORE any consumer change: three new relations are created that nothing reads, so no committed surface can lose a row it could previously reach and no route changes behaviour. The feature gate `admin_workforce_command_v2` is off by default per CP-099, and nothing in this file is reachable from a user-facing surface yet.
execution.idempotency: Deterministic and repeatable. `create table if not exists` for the three relations, `create index if not exists` for all indexes, `create or replace` for both functions and both views, `drop trigger if exists` before each `create trigger`, `drop policy if exists` + `create policy` with a final name for each of the ten policies, `comment on` for each, an explicit grant/revoke block, and a DO block that only reads the catalog and RAISEs. Verified by applying the file EIGHT times on a throwaway PostgreSQL 16.15 cluster in supabase/tests/wfc004_workforce_departments.harness.sh: no error on any apply, and the policy signature over all workforce and vendor relations was byte-identical before and after, measured as a sorted concatenated string. The harness additionally relies on this: it DROPS the one-accountable-manager and one-active-primary indexes to prove each race is enforced by its index, then re-applies THIS FILE to restore them - so if re-application did not restore them, the harness would fail rather than quietly measure a different schema.

quarantine.strategy: No data movement, no backfill, no batch, in this file. The change is three relations, one function, two trigger functions, two triggers, ten policies, two views and a grant block. There is no partial-application state: the file is one transaction and its own post-condition RAISEs if the asserted state is unreachable, so a half-applied policy set cannot be committed. The free-text `department` values and the name-only vendor rows are NOT quarantined here; 20260927100200 records them as reviewable link and quarantine rows, which is the CP-096 shape.
quarantine.lockBudget: Every has_perm, is_org_member and workforce_department_is_managed_by call is wrapped in `(select ...)` so the planner evaluates the SECURITY DEFINER call as an InitPlan once per statement rather than once per row. Their bodies are indexed lookups: has_perm reads org_members by its (org_id, user_id) primary key and org_role_permissions by its role primary key; is_org_member reads org_members by the same key; workforce_department_is_managed_by reads the partial unique index on workforce_department_managers (at most one row) and one indexed lookup on workforce_departments' primary key. The added work versus a target with no workforce tables is the creation of the tables themselves; no existing read path is slowed.

constraints: workforce_departments_id_org_key UNIQUE (id, org_id) - the composite form required to reference (id, org_id) from a child table. It is what makes a manager row, a membership row, a status event and a vendor department all provably inside ONE organization by FOREIGN KEY rather than by a predicate somebody can forget.

workforce_departments_vendor_kind_fkey FOREIGN KEY (vendor_entity_id, org_id) REFERENCES vendor_entities (id, org_id) ON DELETE RESTRICT - a cross-organization VENDOR reference is structurally impossible. MEASURED: a vendor department in org B naming org A's vendor entity is refused 23503, with a positive control that the identical insert with the department's own org_id succeeds. This is acceptance criterion 3 as a database guarantee rather than a policy outcome.

workforce_departments_vendor_required / _vendor_only CHECK - a vendor department OWNS a vendor entity and an internal department never does. BOTH directions are checked, because 'vendor_entity_id is not null implies vendor' is the direction that would otherwise let a department be pointed at a vendor for authorization purposes while presenting as internal.

workforce_departments_org_slug_key UNIQUE (org_id, slug) - per organization, not platform-wide: two organizations may both have a 'production' department, and the resolver's cross-org denial relies on the ID, never on the slug. `organizations.slug` being `text not null unique` (20250816132000:10) is a tenant-uniqueness guarantee on a NAME and WFC-003 §1.4 forbids using it to match organizations; the same reasoning applies here.
workforce_departments_slug_len / _name_len CHECK - a department with an empty name is not a department an operator can select.

workforce_department_managers_department_fkey FOREIGN KEY (department_id, org_id) REFERENCES workforce_departments (id, org_id) ON DELETE CASCADE - MEASURED 23503 for a cross-organization manager row, with a positive control. Cascade here because a deleted department's manager rows are the deleted department's business; the LEDGER restricts instead, and the asymmetry is deliberate and stated in 20260927100200.

workforce_department_managers_window CHECK (ended_at is null or ended_at >= assigned_at) and _end_reason CHECK (ended_at is null or (ended_reason is not null and char_length(btrim(ended_reason)) >= 3)) - CP-094's one-accountable-manager rule is only as good as its audit trail, and a manager row that vanishes with no stated reason is how 'who was accountable in March' becomes unanswerable.

workforce_department_memberships_department_fkey FOREIGN KEY (department_id, org_id) REFERENCES workforce_departments (id, org_id) ON DELETE CASCADE - MEASURED 23503 for a cross-organization membership, with a positive control.

workforce_department_memberships_id_dept_person_key UNIQUE (id, department_id, person_user_id) - exists so 20260927100200's ledger can carry a THREE-column composite foreign key and therefore be structurally incapable of attaching a status to a person who is not in the named department. `id` is already the primary key, so this adds no logical key.
workforce_department_memberships_window CHECK (effective_to is null or effective_to > effective_from) - a membership that ends before it begins is not a history.

The ten policies ARE the authorization boundary, and each arm's reason is on the policy's own COMMENT. Departments: SELECT is org-wide workforce.view OR manage OR managing THIS department; INSERT and DELETE require org-wide workforce.manage only, so a department manager can neither create nor delete a department; UPDATE is symmetric on both clauses and its column boundary is the trigger. Managers: SELECT is the same triple; INSERT and UPDATE require org-wide workforce.manage AND is_org_member on the row's SUBJECT, with no department-scoped arm, and no DELETE policy or privilege. Memberships: SELECT is the same triple OR the worker's own CURRENT rows, bounded to is_active and effective_to is null so it discloses the present placement and not a colleague-visible employment history; INSERT and UPDATE admit org-wide manage OR managing the department named IN THE ROW, so a manager of department A cannot place a membership into department B (MEASURED 42501); no DELETE policy or privilege.
indexes: workforce_department_managers_one_accountable_uidx UNIQUE (department_id) WHERE ended_at IS NULL - THE CP-094 GUARANTEE, and the reason it is an index. Measured: two simultaneous appointments produced 1 row and at least one 23505; with the index dropped a second manager for the same department was accepted. A trigger that SELECTs then INSERTs would not hold this under concurrency. The contract postflight asserts the WHERE clause, not merely the index's existence, because an index that silently lost its predicate stops being a guarantee while still being present.

workforce_department_memberships_one_active_primary_uidx UNIQUE (org_id, person_user_id) WHERE membership_kind = 'primary' AND is_active AND effective_to IS NULL - THE CP-094 GUARANTEE, same construction and same proof, same drop-the-index control. Partial so an ended primary and historical rows do not collide with the current one.

workforce_department_memberships_person_department_uidx UNIQUE (department_id, person_user_id, membership_kind) WHERE is_active AND effective_to IS NULL - a different guarantee from the one above and not implied by it: at most one ACTIVE row of each kind per department.

recovery.forwardFix: Any correction is a new additive migration with a higher version carrying DROP/CREATE for these relations. Three forward-fix shapes are worth naming in advance. labelledProbes: PROBE 1, EXPECTED their organization's rows: an organization administrator reads every department in their own organization and 0 in any other. A non-zero count in another organization is a P0 and means the composite conjuncts or has_perm are not being applied.

PROBE 2, EXPECTED 1 affected row: a department manager who IS an appointed manager renames their own department. This is CP-094's resource scope and it is the assertion that the symmetric-with-trigger design exists for. A 42501 here means the policy has been made asymmetric and the legitimate write is broken.
PROBE 3, EXPECTED 42501 naming the three protected columns: the same manager updates department_kind and vendor_entity_id on their own department. A silent success is a cross-tenant escalation.

PROBE 4, EXPECTED `UPDATE 0` and exit 0: a secondary-only member updates a department they do not manage. READ THE ROW COUNT, NOT THE EXIT CODE. This is the silent-no-op fact and a caller that checks only the exit code will report success.

PROBE 5, EXPECTED 42501: a secondary-only member inserts a workforce_department_managers row for themselves. Any success means the manager INSERT policy has gained a department-scoped arm and CP-094 part 3(b) is false.

PROBE 6, EXPECTED 23503 on workforce_department_managers_department_fkey, workforce_department_memberships_department_fkey and workforce_departments_vendor_kind_fkey respectively: three cross-organization inserts, each paired with the identical insert at the correct org_id as a positive control. A 23505 instead of a 23503 means the one-accountable-manager index answered first and the tenant check was not exercised.

PROBE 7, EXPECTED FALSE: `select workforce_department_is_managed_by('<a secondary-only member>', '<their department>')` after the same call returns TRUE for the appointed manager. Both are required - a FALSE for everyone is a predicate that never fires.

PROBE 8, EXPECTED FALSE for a revoked manager whose row is still open: set a member's org_members.status to 'revoked' without ending their manager row. A TRUE here is the seven-sites fail-open pattern WFC-003 §2.3a records, reproduced.

PROBE 9, EXPECTED 42501 from the trigger as a privileged writer: insert a manager row for a user with no org_members row, executed as the table owner or as service_role. RLS is not the only writer, and a policy-only check is bypassable here.
